title: Woodblock
when: Water, weather, journeys, slow forces and quiet drama: a story told like a print from a series of views

voice.style: calm, spare and observant, a little formal

rules: Flat colour inside an ink key line; depth comes from overlap and scale, never from glow.
Skies and water carry bokashi: a gradient from accent (Prussian blue) into the paper, top to bottom. One gradient per area.
Water and shading are cut lines: print {screen: lines, ink: accent, angle: -20} on the sea, swelling where it darkens. Start from the woodblock-wave sketch.
Compose off-centre with a strong diagonal and a small, distant subject (a mountain, a boat, a figure) so scale tells the story.
A cartouche (a small accent2 rectangle with a title in serif) may name the view; nothing else is lettered on the picture.
